title: T-plurals that use KPT
summary: Change the consonant stem first and add plural -t second.
objectives: Identify the KPT change in a plural.
Add -t only after the stem is ready.

sections.title: Two construction steps
paragraphs: Many nouns use the weak KPT grade before nominative plural -t. First build the weak stem; then add the plural ending.
Keeping the steps separate makes the form easier to understand: noun → weak stem → plural.

sections.title: The same familiar KPT pairs
paragraphs: The changes are the same ones introduced earlier: double consonants can shorten, a single p can become v, and clusters can change.
The final -t is the plural ending. A t created inside the stem is not the plural ending.

steps: Use the known change kk → k: pankki → panki-.
Add the known plural ending -t: pankit.
Use the known change pp → p: kauppa → kaupa-.
Add the known plural ending -t: kaupat.

commonMistakes: Do not attach -t to the unchanged dictionary form when KPT is required.
Do not count the final plural -t as part of the KPT change.
Use the learned stem for that word; spelling cannot always be guessed from English.

practiceExercises.explanation: First use kk → k: panki-. Then add plural -t: pankit.
kauppa uses pp → p in the weak stem kaupa-. Add -t: kaupat.
First change lt → ll to make pello-. Then add plural -t: pellot.
